## 1\. Munnar – A Hill Station Retreat Amidst Tea Gardens

If there's one place in Kerala that manages to capture the heart of every traveller irrespective of their interests, it's Munnar. Embraced by sprawling tea plantations, cool mountain breeze and breathtaking scenery, this dreamy hill station sits at an altitude of 1,600 meters above sea level.

Whether you're a honeymooner looking for romance, a nature lover seeking serenity, or an adventure enthusiast craving excitement, Munnar welcomes you with its misty hills, lush green valleys, and soothing breeze.

### Things to Do in Munnar, Kerala:

- Visit the Tea Museum to learn about tea processing
- Explore the Eravikulam National Park and spot Nilgiri Tahr
- Take a scenic drive to Top Station for panoramic views
- Enjoy boating at Kundala Lake

## 2\. Alleppey & Kumarakom – The Backwaters Paradise

Alleppey (Alappuzha) and Kumarakom are famous for their enchanting backwaters, making them among the best tourist places in Kerala. A houseboat cruise through these serene waters is an experience you should not miss. The labyrinth of canals, coconut groves, and floating villages create an unforgettable setting, ideal for relaxation and rejuvenation.

### Things to Do in Alleppey & Kumarakom, Kerala:

- Stay overnight on a luxury houseboat
- Visit the Kumarakom Bird Sanctuary
- Experience the traditional Snake Boat Race (if visiting during Onam)
- Enjoy a relaxing Ayurvedic spa by the backwaters

## 3\. Wayanad – A Blend of Waterfalls and Wildlife

Wayanad, nestled in the Western Ghats, is a dream destination for nature lovers and adventure seekers. With its lush forests, misty hills, and rich wildlife, it’s a top pick for those exploring tourist places in Kerala. The region boasts charming villages, spice plantations, and cultural sites that make it a perfect mix of relaxation and exploration.

### Things to Do in Wayanad, Kerala:

- Trek to the Edakkal Caves to see ancient carvings
- Visit the Meenmutty and Soochipara waterfalls
- Explore the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary
- Camp near Banasura Sagar Dam, India’s largest earthen dam

## 4\. Thekkady – Home to Periyar National Park

Thekkady is one of Kerala's most fascinating tourist destinations for those who love animals. The Periyar National Park is an exciting place to visit because of its rich biodiversity and lush forests. The area is a sensory joy and is well-known for its fragrant spice crops.

### Things to Do in Thekkady, Kerala:

- Enjoy a boat safari in Periyar Lake to spot elephants and tigers
- Take a guided nature walk through the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary
- Experience bamboo rafting for an adventurous touch
- Visit the spice plantations for an aromatic experience

## 5\. Vagamon – Offbeat Hill Station and Camping Delight

If you are looking for an offbeat experience, Vagamon is an underrated yet stunning hill station in Kerala. Nestled amidst lush greenery, mist-covered valleys, and rolling meadows, it offers a perfect blend of adventure and tranquility. Vagamon maintains its natural beauty in contrast to the more commercialised hill stations, which makes it the perfect retreat for hikers, nature enthusiasts, and anyone looking for tranquilly away from the bustle of the city.

### Things to Do in Vagamon, Kerala:

- Try paragliding for a bird’s-eye view of the valley
- Visit the Pine Forests for a serene escape
- Experience camping under the stars with Exoticamp
- Explore the scenic Vagamon Meadows and Tea Estates

The ideal option for escaping into nature is with [Exoticamp's Vagamon Camping](https://www.exoticamp.com/camping/vagamon-camp-above-the-clouds) Experience. Imagine enjoying the comforts of a bonfire in the evenings while lodging in cosy tents amid the tranquil beauty of the hills. Enjoy breathtaking views of the sunrise and clean mountain air as you awaken. This camping experience offers a special opportunity to peacefully and immersively interact with nature, regardless of your preference for action or relaxation.

## 6\. Kochi – The Cultural Capital of Kerala

Cochin, another name for Kochi, is one of Kerala's most popular tourist destinations, fusing modernism with a wealth of historical influences. The city is charming because of its colonial architecture, vibrant marketplaces, breathtaking coastline, and intriguing blend of British, Portuguese, and Dutch traditions.

### Things to Do in Kochi, Kerala:

- Visit Fort Kochi for its Portuguese-style buildings
- Watch a Kathakali dance performance
- Explore the Jewish Synagogue and Mattancherry Palace
- Enjoy a scenic sunset at Marine Drive
- Try authentic Kerala cuisine at a local restaurant

## 7\. Gavi – An Eco-Tourism Haven

With its unspoiled forests, stunning scenery, and tranquil environment, Gavi is a hidden treasure among Kerala's tourist destinations. This ecotourism destination, which is part of the Periyar Tiger Reserve, is ideal for adventurers and nature lovers who want to get away from the bustle of the city.

### Things to Do in Gavi, Kerala:

- Take a jeep safari through the dense forests
- Go for a nature trek to spot exotic flora and fauna
- Enjoy a boat ride in Gavi Lake
- Visit the Sabarimala viewpoint for mesmerizing views

## 8\. Varkala – A Beach Lover’s Paradise

For beach enthusiasts, Varkala is one of Kerala's top tourist destinations. Varkala is a distinctive and beautiful location that stands out from other Keralan beaches due to its striking red laterite cliffs that border the Arabian Sea. It's the ideal retreat for backpackers, couples, and single people because of its lively cafes, peaceful beaches, and spiritual atmosphere.

### Things to Do in Varkala, Kerala:

- Relax at Varkala Beach, also known as Papanasam Beach
- Take a dip in the natural spring, believed to have medicinal properties
- Visit the ancient Janardanaswamy Temple
- Explore the cafés and beach shacks for a laid-back vibe

## 9\. Bekal – A Coastal Gem with a Historic Fort

Bekal, located in northern Kerala, is famous for its Bekal Fort, one of the largest and best-preserved forts in the state. TWith its enormous walls and keyhole-shaped structure, the fort provides stunning sweeping vistas of the Arabian Sea and has served as a backdrop for a number of Bollywood productions. Bekal is the perfect place for history aficionados, beach lovers, and photographers because of its tranquil atmosphere and historical significance.

### Things to Do in Bekal, Kerala:

- Explore the Bekal Fort and its scenic surroundings
- Relax at Bekal Beach
- Visit the Chandragiri Fort for historical insights
- Enjoy a houseboat ride through the Valiyaparamba backwaters

## 10\. Athirapally Falls – The Niagara of India

No list of tourist places in Kerala is complete without mentioning Athirapally Falls, the largest waterfall in Kerala. This magnificent waterfall, which rises to a height of 80 feet and is encircled by thick rainforests, is a breathtaking sight, particularly during the rainy season. Athirapally's nickname comes from the water's overwhelming force and the surrounding lush flora, which evoke the majesty of Niagara Falls.

### Things to Do in Athirapally, Kerala:

- Witness the spectacular Athirapally and Vazhachal Falls
- Explore the Sholayar Forests for a refreshing nature walk
- Visit the Charpa Falls, a lesser-known yet beautiful cascade
- Enjoy a scenic drive through the lush greenery

### 11\. Kovalam – A Coastal Escape with Pristine Beaches

One of the most well-known beaches in Kerala is Kovalam, which is well-known for its crescent-shaped shoreline, swaying coconut palms, and exciting nightlife. Kovalam provides the ideal fusion of leisure, exploration, and cultural encounters thanks to its three nearby beaches: Lighthouse Beach, Hawah Beach, and Samudra Beach.

### Things to Do in Kovalam, Kerala:

- Sunbathe at Lighthouse Beach
- Enjoy water sports like surfing and parasailing
- Visit the Vizhinjam Marine Aquarium
- Experience an Ayurvedic massage at a seaside resort in Kovalam

### 12\. Trivandrum – The Capital City with a Cultural Touch

Thiruvananthapuram (Trivandrum), the capital of Kerala, seamlessly blends cultural heritage, natural beauty, and modern attractions. From centuries-old temples to serene beaches and vibrant museums, Trivandrum offers a well-rounded experience for travelers.

### Things to Do in Trivandrum, Kerala:

- Visit the iconic Padmanabhaswamy Temple
- Explore the Napier Museum and Sri Chitra Art Gallery
- Relax at Shangumugham Beach
- Take a tour of the Kerala Science and Technology Museum

### 13\. Thrissur – The Cultural Hub of Kerala

Thrissur, often called the ‘Cultural Capital of Kerala,’ is a city steeped in history and tradition. It is famous for its temples, classical arts, and vibrant festivals, particularly the grand Thrissur Pooram.

### Things to Do in Thrissur, Kerala:

- Witness the grand Thrissur Pooram festival (April-May)
- Visit Vadakkunnathan Temple
- Explore the Kerala Kalamandalam for traditional arts
- Relax at Athirappilly Waterfalls, located nearby

### 14\. Idukki – A Land of Hills and Dams

Idukki, a paradise for nature lovers, is known for its rolling hills, wildlife sanctuaries, and impressive hydroelectric projects. The region offers breathtaking views and serene landscapes, making it perfect destination in Kerala for adventure seekers and peace lovers alike.

### Things to Do in Idukki, Kerala:

- Visit the Idukki Arch Dam, India’s first and Asia’s biggest arch dam
- Explore the Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary
- Enjoy a scenic drive through the tea gardens of Idukki
- Trek to Meesapulimala for breathtaking views

### 15\. Palakkad – The Gateway to Kerala’s Natural Beauty

Palakkad, also known as the ‘Rice Bowl of Kerala,’ is famous for its lush landscapes, historical sites, and serene environment. The city serves as a vital link between Kerala and Tamil Nadu, offering a blend of cultural heritage and natural beauty.

### Things to Do in Palakkad, Kerala:

- Explore the Palakkad Fort
- Visit the Silent Valley National Park
- Take a boat ride in Malampuzha Dam
- Discover the traditional village life in Kollengode

### 16\. Kozhikode – A Blend of History and Cuisine

Kozhikode (Calicut) is a coastal city known for its rich history, beautiful beaches, and delicious Malabar cuisine. Once a major trading hub for spices in Kerala, the city offers a unique mix of colonial influences and local culture.

### Things to Do in Kozhikode, Kerala:

- Visit Kappad Beach, where Vasco da Gama landed in 1498
- Explore the Mananchira Square and Kozhikode Beach
- Taste authentic Malabar biryani
- Discover the historical Pazhassi Raja Museum

### 17\. Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary – A Haven for Nature Lovers

Located in the rain shadow region of the Western Ghats, Chinnar Wildlife Sanctuary is one of Kerala’s most unique ecological zones, known for its dry deciduous forests, wildlife, and tribal settlements.

### Things to Do in Chinnar, Kerala:

- Go on a guided jungle safari to spot endangered species like the grizzled giant squirrel
- Trek through the scenic trails
- Visit the Thoovanam Waterfalls inside the sanctuary
- Enjoy birdwatching in the rich biodiversity zone

### 18\. Ponmudi – A Hidden Hill Station with Breathtaking Views

Ponmudi, meaning "Golden Peak," is a picturesque hill station in the Western Ghats. Known for its winding roads, lush green tea estates, and mist-covered hills, it’s a perfect getaway in Kerala for nature lovers and adventure seekers.

### Things to Do in Ponmudi, Kerala:

- Trek to Agasthyarkoodam, one of the highest peaks in Kerala
- Visit Meenmutty Waterfalls for a refreshing experience
- Enjoy a scenic drive through the 22 hairpin bends leading to Ponmudi
- Explore Peppara Wildlife Sanctuary for an offbeat adventure

### 19\. Malampuzha – The Perfect Blend of Nature and Adventure

Kerala's largest reservoir is located in the picturesque town of Malampuzha, which is part of Palakkad and offers a variety of gardens, dams, and adventure activities. Families and anyone who enjoy the outdoors will love this place.

### Things to Do in Malampuzha, Kerala:

- Visit the famous Malampuzha Dam and Gardens
- Take a ropeway ride for stunning aerial views
- Explore the Rock Garden, created by renowned artist Nek Chand
- Enjoy a boat ride in Malampuzha Reservoir

### 20\. Munroe Island – An Offbeat Backwater Destination

A hidden jewel in Kerala's backwaters, Munroe Island provides a peaceful haven with picturesque canals, verdant coconut plantations, and a traditional village way of life. It's a fantastic substitute for the busier backwater locations like Alleppey.

### Things to Do in Munroe Island, Kerala:

- Experience a serene canoe tour through the narrow canals
- Witness the unique Kallada Boat Race during the Onam festival
- Visit the historic Dutch Church
- Enjoy a traditional Kerala village stay for an authentic experience

### Best Time to Visit Kerala

Kerala is a year-round destination, but the best time to visit depends on what kind of experience you're looking for.

#### 1\. Winter (October to February) – Best Season to Visit

This is the peak tourist season in Kerala, offering pleasant weather and cool breezes, making it perfect for sightseeing, backwater cruises, and beach vacations.

**Why visit in winter?**

- Comfortable temperatures (20°C to 30°C)
- Ideal for houseboat cruises in Alleppey and Kumarakom
- Best time for hill station getaways in Munnar, Wayanad, and Thekkady
- Perfect for exploring cultural and heritage sites in Kochi and Thrissur

#### 2\. Summer (March to May) – Ideal for Hill Stations

While the coastal areas experience high humidity, hill stations in Kerala like Munnar, Vagamon, and Idukki remain pleasant. This is one of the best times to book Ayurvedic resorts and enjoy rejuvenating treatments, wellness retreats, and traditional healing practices.

**Why visit in summer?**

- Less crowded tourist spots
- Cooler temperatures in hill stations
- Great time for trekking and nature walks
- Off-season discounts on accommodations and packages

#### 3\. Monsoon (June to September) – Best for Ayurveda & Nature Lovers

Kerala receives heavy rainfall, making the landscapes lush and refreshing. It is the best time to indulge in Ayurvedic treatments and witness the beauty of the backwaters in their full glory.

**Why visit in monsoon?**

- Best time for Ayurvedic therapies and spa retreats
- Mesmerizing views of waterfalls like Athirapally and Meenmutty
- Greenest landscapes and fewer tourists
- Experience the famous Onam festival in August/September

## Conclusion

Kerala offers a wealth of breathtaking scenery, a vibrant culture, and exhilarating experiences. This lovely state offers something for everyone, whether you're searching for a wildlife adventure in Thekkady, a romantic houseboat vacation in Alleppey, or a hill station retreat in Munnar. Kerala is a must-visit location for tourists from all over the world since each of these tourist attractions delivers a distinctive experience.

So, pack your bags and get ready to explore God’s Own Country!

pages.title: Fun things to do in Japan
pages.summary: Japan is one of the most exciting destination to explore that it can be overwhelming to decide what to do, here is my selection...
pages.content:
Welcome to Japan, a country famous for its ancient traditions and advanced technology. Once you land in Tokyo or Osaka, it’s impossible not to find fun things to do during your holidays. From the majestic views of Mount Fuji and the sumptuous Shinto shrines in Kyoto or Nikko to pristine beaches to relax all over the Okinawa Archipelago, the hardest thing is to choose what to do! Considered one of the [safest diving destinations in the world](https://worldadventuredivers.com/safe-places-travel-alone/), the country of the rising sun, and especially its southern prefecture, Okinawa, is one of the favourite places to go for ocean lovers who are into surfing or scuba diving.

At world-class dive sites such as Yonaguni Monument, Manta City, or the Kerama National Park, you will be able to see turtles, hammerhead sharks, and manta rays or experience wreck diving. But there are so many other things to do besides [diving in Japan](https://worldadventuredivers.com/destinations/asia/japan/), like trying some local food, relaxing in a hot spring bath, or even visiting an interactive digital exhibition that will blow your mind. Here are 15 of my favourite activities to do in Japan as a scuba diver for you to find some inspiration. Note that most of these activities include places below 600 m of altitude. Still, for the few locations which are above, altitude is indicated so you can safely plan your itinerary between scuba diving and sightseeing during your stay in Japan.

## 1 – Chasing the best views of Mount Fuji in Kawaguchiko, Yamanashi

![Mount Fuji above Kawaguchiko Lake Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/IMG_1774ra.jpg?w=2000&ssl=1)

Mount Fuji above Kawaguchiko Lake Japan

Admiring the majestic Mount Fuji, the highest peak in Japan with 3776 m of altitude, is on any visitor to do list. However, seeing Japan’s most famous volcano can be trickier than it sounds. Indeed, fog and clouds often cover the iconic Japanese peak, which can even be seen from Tokyo on a clear day. The best time is to get up early, since visibility is usually better in the morning.

Some of the best views of Mount Fuji, called “Fujisan” in Japanese, are located on its northern side, in the region of the five lakes around the town of Kawaguchiko. In the spring, when the cherry tree blossoms, or in the fall, when the maple trees turn red, catching a shot of Mount Fuji and its reflection on Kawaguchi Lake or Motosu Lake through the branches is the promise of a killer shot (for information, Kawaguchiko is above 800 m in altitude). Still, in the same area, Chureito Pagoda is maybe one of the most famous sights in Japan, with its gracious red pagoda and Mount Fuji (if lucky) in the background.

But if managing through the clouds wasn’t enough, planning for nature’s blossoms or autumn colours can be even trickier at higher altitudes. For instance, I visited Kawaguchiko two weeks too early for cherry blossom, but I think it’s part of the fun. As a rule of thumb, you can keep in mind mid-April for cherry blossom and mid-October for “momiji” leaves in Kawaguchiko.

While I enjoyed spending a couple of days in Kawaguchiko to find all the best viewpoints, if you’re short on time, you can book a [private tour from Tokyo](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/1fbF7Gdq) to see them all in one day!

## 2 – Swimming with turtles in the Kerama National Park, Okinawa

![snorkelling with turtles Tokashiki Okinawa](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/IMG_5259rc_D.jpeg?w=2000&ssl=1)

snorkelling with turtles Tokashiki Okinawa

The Kerama Shoto National Park is one of the reasons why [scuba diving in Okinawa](https://worldadventuredivers.com/scuba-diving-okinawa-first-time/) became famous. Directly accessible from Naha thanks to daily ferries and scuba diving charter boats, it is surprisingly easy to visit as a scuba diver or even an enthusiastic snorkeler.

The islands are fantastic natural havens with paradise-like beaches and great snorkelling, which you won’t find on the main island of Okinawa. Depending on the time you have to visit the Kerama Islands, you may have to choose between Zamami, Aka, and Tokashiki, the three main islands of the park. Tokashiki Island is the closest to Naha; it only takes 35 minutes to cross over, while it takes about an hour to get to Aka and Zamam, which are on the same ferry line. Learn more about the best way to start [planning a trip to Okinawa](https://worldadventuredivers.com/planning-trip-okinawa/).

There are beautiful dive sites all around the islands of the park, but I have a personal preference for the sites on the west coast of Tokashiki near Aaren Beach. However, as I stayed on both Zamami and Takashiki islands, I could go [snorkelling with turtles](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/dWIvch3n) early in the morning directly from the beach at Ama Beach and Tokashiku Beach, respectively. Unforgettable!

## 3 – Diving with manta rays in Ishigaki, Okinawa

![Manta rays diving in Ishigaki Okinawa - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/IMG_9760.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Manta rays diving in Ishigaki Okinawa - fun things to do in Japan

Ishigaki is another scuba diving highlight of the Okinawa Prefecture, thanks to its resident manta ray,s which can be seen all year round. Be aware that the best spots for [diving with manta rays in Ishigaki](https://worldadventuredivers.com/diving-ishigaki/) are near Kabira Bay, between April and October. As the winds change during wintertime, manta rays can still be found southward in the waters of Kuroshima or Iriomote islands.

Beyond scuba diving, the “Stonewall” island offers a perfect balance of peaceful nature and lively culture. Thanks to the numerous ferries linking the Yaeyama Islands, even you won’t be able to visit them all, but don’t miss the opportunity to explore Taketomi-Jima. It is only 10 minutes away. This is the loveliest and most preserved island I got to visit in the entire Okinawa Prefecture.

## 4 – Exploring an ancient sunken city in Yonaguni, Okinawa

![Yonaguni Monument diving Okinawa - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/IMG_0205.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Yonaguni Monument diving Okinawa - fun things to do in Japan

Yonaguni is simply the most legendary spot in Okinawa and Japan for scuba divers. It is usually the reason people first hear about scuba diving in Okinawa. Yonaguni is the westernmost island of Japan and is actually closer to Taiwan, being just a bit more than 100 km away. With its endemic horse species and green grass ranches, it isn’t the regular tropical island you would expect.

The main highlight of Yonaguni is its underwater monument, called Kaitei Iseki in Japanese. Some call it the Yonaguni Monument, others the sunken city of Yonaguni, surrounded by myths and conflicting scientific studies; the truth is, nobody knows for sure what this massive stone formation is. In any case, you won’t be disappointed as this is a once-in-a-lifetime drift dive!

On top of this, between January and March, if you are an experienced diver with at least 100 dives, you may give it a try to see the hammerhead sharks when [diving in Yonaguni](https://worldadventuredivers.com/diving-yonaguni/). Be aware that I saw them five times out of nine, so being patient and persistent is usually required.

## 5 – Soaking in hot springs in the Izu Peninsula, Shizuoka

![Tatto friendly onsen Ryokan Tokyo in Yugawara - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/IMG_7274.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Tatto friendly onsen Ryokan Tokyo in Yugawara - fun things to do in Japan

If I had to keep only one thing to do in Japan, it would be soaking in a natural hot spring (“onsen”) outside while a snowflake falls on my nose! While I had this experience after visiting the snow monkeys in Nagano Prefecture, my best onsen experiences were in Yugawara, Kanagawa Prefecture, and in Ito, Shizuoka Prefecture, as I was [scuba diving in the Izu Peninsula](https://worldadventuredivers.com/izu-peninsula-diving/).

They are usually fully equipped facilities with lockers and all the soap, shampoo, conditioner and hairdryer you may need. I enjoyed taking my shower and resting in the hot spring bath so much that I would use it each morning and each evening whenever I stayed in a ryokan (traditional Japanese inn), which are usually built around one. We’re never too clean, right?

The water can be hot, ranging from 38°C to 42°C, so it can be more or less challenging to get in or stay in for long. As the water from the spring continuously flows into the hot spring bath, no chlorine is used, leaving the skin incredibly soft. Each volcanic hot spring has different mineral concentrations and hence different healing properties. This is such a good excuse to try as many as possible, right?

Here are the list of hotels and ryokan where I enjoyed the most my “onsen” experience:

- [The Ryokan Tokyo](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/the-ryokan-tokyo-yugawara.html?aid=908126&no_rooms=1&group_adults=1&room1=A) in Yugawara
- [K’s House](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/historical-ryokan-hostel-k-s-house-ito-onsen.en.html?aid=908126&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2) in Ito
- [Minshuku Miyama](https://www.booking.com/hotel/jp/minshuku-miyama.en.html?aid=908126&no_rooms=1&group_adults=2) in Yamanouchi

## 6 – Eat delicious sushi without breaking the bank at a kaiten sushi restaurant

![Kaiten sushi Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_8459.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Kaiten sushi Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan

Thanks to the “kaiten” sushi restaurants, the budget traveller can enjoy quality sushi at the best price. The kaiten is a rotating conveyor belt that presents different types of sushis the sushi chefs have freshly prepared. You just need to pick the plate you like, and you will pay based on the plate’s colour and how many you eat.

The Hamazushi chain has restaurants all over Japan. I loved their concept so much that I went to their addresses in Tokyo, Ito and even Naha, in Okinawa. Their average price, 150¥ for 2 nigiri sushi, is so affordable that I usually end up with a bill of 800 to 1000¥ (about 7 to 9€)! The address in Tokyo is 24-8 Udagawachō, 2 Chome−13, Takadanobaba.

To go beyond just eating, you can take the experience a tad further and book a [sushi-making class](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/ofMogQ0u) in Tokyo!

## 7 – Wearing a kimono while visiting Kyoto’s most beautiful temples

![wearing a yukata - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/06/IMG_7133.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

wearing a yukata - fun things to do in Japan

I didn’t plan for it, but the first thing I ever did in Japan was to [rent a kimono in Kyoto](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/1IhkkL2C), thinking I was purchasing one! While it was before I could communicate in Japanese, I should have known that kimonos are so expensive that the 50€ I paid could only be for a rental! If you think this is expensive, first, yes, it is dear, but you can find places which do it for cheaper. However, even if I felt a bit stupid for not understanding, it remains one of my favourite experiences ever in Japan, as it included nearly 30 minutes of elaborate dressing up in a real silk kimono, not a cotton yukata!

You can keep the kimono for the entire day and take photos in the most beautiful temples of Kyoto, such as the Kiyomizu-dera, Fushimi-Inari or the Kinkyaku-ji. Note, you can also [rent a kimono in Tokyo](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/5Y0HY2rQ) and go to the Senso-ji Temple in the Asakusa district.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 8 – Being blown away by the Borderless digital exhibition, Tokyo

![Teamlab borderless digital art museum Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_7606.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Teamlab borderless digital art museum Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan

It wasn’t something I necessarily had on my list while exploring Japan, but this exhibition literally blew my mind. Somewhere between an arty digital experience and a new-generation amusement park, the [TeamLab Borderless exhibition](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/zg4JvVFL) takes you to a new dimension where you can play with digital and interactive art.

Make sure to plan to arrive at least 15 minutes before the opening time in the morning for a more enjoyable experience. You can spend the entire day inside if you want to experience everything fully. I recommend not missing the waterfall and the lamp room. The place is a maze, so take your time not to miss anything!

## 9 – Celebrate Hanami with a picnic under the cherry blossom trees

![Nakameguro River Sakura in Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_2361.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Nakameguro River Sakura in Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan

I understand now why everyone gets crazy about sakura, the celebrated little cherry flowers in the spring, usually in the first half of April. It is indeed beautiful, but it is also the peak tourist season from Tokyo to Kyoto. When [visiting Tokyo](https://worldadventuredivers.com/tokyo-layover-guide/), the top spots to see sakura are the Nakameguro River and Chidorigafuchi Greenway near the Imperial Palace. Get there early in the morning, or you can also visit these famous areas late at night, as the spectacle is equally enchanting thanks to the lighting systems.

The sakura season is also the time of one of Japan’s most beloved events: Hanami. People gather for picnics during the daytime or at night to share drinks and snacks, if possible, pink and sakura flavoured. You will find everything you need in all the supermarkets, from the tarp to put on the grass to the delicious sakura mochis.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 10 – Admiring the Autumn colours of the “momiji” maple leaves in Nikko

![Momiji Automn leaves - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/IMG_7993.jpg?w=2000&ssl=1)

Momiji Automn leaves - fun things to do in Japan

Even if the sakura season is delightful, Fall and the “momiji” season, when the maple leaves turn bright red, and the ginkgo leaves turn bright yellow, are my absolute favourite seasons in Japan. Be careful with timing: at altitude, the season starts earlier, so plan to go mid-October, but in places by the sea, like Tokyo, it begins as late as the beginning of December.

I have spent days and days photographing the Autumn leaves at any given opportunity, as I found it mesmerising, especially at the beginning when you have a mix of green, yellow and red leaves. My top locations to see momiji leaves and take pictures were the Shinjuku Park and Koishikawa Garden in Tokyo, Yugawara in Kanagawa Prefecture and Shuzenji in Shizuoka Prefecture.

Still, Nikko and its UNESCO World Heritage Toshogu Shrine was just another level of stunning as I visited it at the beginning of November. The Shrine itself is mostly in a pine tree forest, but near the entrance, the Treasure Museum has a gorgeous garden full of maple trees. For the full autumn colours show in the wild, take the bus to Lake Chuzenji and Kegon Waterfalls. Note that, as it is higher in altitude (1269 m), you will need to get there earlier, mid to end of October. It is possible to book a [private tour from Tokyo](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/hbBL2Zie) to make the most of a day trip to Nikko.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 11 – Meeting with the snow monkeys in Jigokudani Park, Nagano

![Jigokudani Snow Monkey Park Nagano Prefecture - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/IMG_9133.jpg?w=2000&ssl=1)

Jigokudani Snow Monkey Park Nagano Prefecture - fun things to do in Japan

If you are lucky enough to visit Japan in the wintertime when snow falls on the Japanese Alps of the Nagano Prefecture, there is one place you must see: the [Snow Monkey Jigokudani Park](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/i0pb4CXz). While it takes several trains or buses to get there from Tokyo and a long walk along an icy trail for a total of 3 to 4 hours, seeing Japanese fluffy monkeys soaking in hot springs with snow all around is just so unique that you won’t regret it.

Take the opportunity to stay in the town of Yamanouchi at a traditional ryokan for a hot-spring bath (for humans!) surrounded by snow, and taste some of the best sake, soba noodles, and chestnuts from the area. By the way, don’t forget the snow monkey park is at 850 m of altitude.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 12 – Choosing your favourite skyline views of Tokyo

![Tokyo Tower view at sunset from WTC Hamamatsucho Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_8560.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Tokyo Tower view at sunset from WTC Hamamatsucho Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan

Visiting one of the many Tokyo observatories should be on your list of places to visit in Tokyo, even if you have only a short stopover. Considering the number of free options, I don’t recommend Roppongi Hills (1800¥/2300¥) & Tokyo Sky Tree (2060¥/3090¥). I find their entrance cost outrageous. I visited the observatory at Roppongi Hills during my very first trip to Japan. I don’t think the view was that much better than the other places, including the free options at the Tokyo Metropolitan Towers or the Bunkyo Civic Centre, which are already excellent viewpoints.

I recommend going to the World Trade Centre in Hamamatsuchō (620¥ – about 5€). At the 40th floor, the [Seaside Top observatory](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/Nywmg8nV) offers the best view in town, with the Tokyo Tower in the middle of Tokyo’s skyline. The observation deck is stylish and comfortable. While the straight windows make a lot of reflection, it’s important to note that it is one of the rare places where tripods are allowed.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 13 – Ordering a matcha latte at a maid café in Akihabara, Tokyo

![Maid café Akihabara Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_7464.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Maid café Akihabara Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan

If you are a fan of manga and/or video games, the Akihabara District is the place you need to go to while in Tokyo. Even if you are not, the “electrical town” (nicknamed for its numerous neon lights) is still a fantastic area to visit, especially if this is your first time in Japan. Wander around the electronics and manga-inspired goodies shops, before daring to push the door of the other speciality of Akihabara. For information, this is where the [Go Kart tours](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/um5VcUIy), inspired by Mario Kart, became famous before spreading across Japan!

The Otaku Mecca is also famous for its maid cafés. At places such as [@Home Café](https://tripadvisor.tpo.li/LY5f9Wjs), you can enjoy all the most “kawaii” (cute) culture of Japan, as girls dress up in cute maid costumes and serve adorable (but overpriced) food and drinks. Some people love it, others hate it. I can’t help it, but I like the place’s positive vibe and the cute drawing on my hot matcha latte, with J-pop music in the background.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 14 – Swimming at the most beautiful beach in Japan, on Miyako Island

![best beaches on Miyakojima - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/IMG_9528-scaled.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

best beaches on Miyakojima - fun things to do in Japan

The sand is so white and thin, the water so clear and blue, that even if I could visit all the beaches around Japan, Yonaha Maehama Beach on the south shore of [Miyako Island](https://worldadventuredivers.com/miyakojima-2/) would have to be the most fabulous beach where you can go swimming in Japan. A hint that I may be right was seeing newlyweds taking their wedding pictures every 15 minutes, with the fabulous shades of blue and turquoise in the background.

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

## 15 – Learning Japanese in Japan at a language school

![Caffe latte art Harajuku Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan](https://i0.wp.com/worldadventuredivers.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/02/IMG_8704.jpg?w=2048&ssl=1)

Caffe latte art Harajuku Tokyo - fun things to do in Japan

From 2018 to 2019, I lived and dived in Japan for a total period of 8 months. For 4 months, [I studied Japanese](https://worldadventuredivers.com/diving-japan-learning-japanese/) at a language school in Tokyo, which was a childhood dream. For a total cost of 2300€ (which wasn’t the cheapest nor the most expensive), learning to communicate autonomously in Japanese dramatically improved my experience in Japan, since outside big cities like Tokyo or Okinawa, very few people can speak English.

I can now book my hotel rooms and dives all over Japan by email or phone without help, and I can order the best food at the best price in a restaurant while making new friends!

![](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)

**Are you looking for more inspiration for fun things to do in other safe travel destinations?**

**If so, have a look at these additional pages:**

- [Fun things to do in French Polynesia](https://worldadventuredivers.com/fun-things-french-polynesia/)
- [Fun things to do in Hawaii](https://worldadventuredivers.com/fun-things-hawaii/)

pages.title: Best Places to Visit in Goa, India
pages.summary: Although Goa has been the 'hottest' goto destination for tourist, there is a lot more to do in Goa than just the hippie relaxed beaches.
pages.content:
There are people who in spite of planning this in your every year’s wish list are not able to make to Goa. And then there are people like me who swear every year that this is the last time I am coming. But then end up there again… for the sixth time.

I don’t really know what is it with fate and Goa is that it cannot let me go and I find myself giving in to those photogenic coconut trees, glittering blue water, and homely Israeli cafes with live music and hippie dancing.

There is just so much to do here. If you feel that there are only bikinis and beaches in Goa, (and there are a lot of fantastic ones), then let me show you more. Goa is a culture. It’s a lifestyle that people from different parts of the world gradually fashioned over the decades.

It hosts various communities, and it’s a temporary home to numerous nomads who come to stay here either or a weekend or for months together.

![A travel guide to Goa, India](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_1.jpg)

A travel guide to Goa, India

## Where to Stay in Goa

Now, this is going to depend upon where would you like to stay, your budget and the facilities you need. But just so that you know, Goa has everything. If you are looking to party and experience the nightlife, I suggest you stay in North Goa near the popular beaches like Calangute or Baga. If you are looking for a view and a quiet time, head to South Goa around Palolem Beach.

**Hotels in North Goa:** [Casa Severina Hotel](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=237504), [Olive Hotel Calangute Niwasa by Embassy Group](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=36123200), [Hotel Sea Castle](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=64536196)

**Hotels in South Goa:** [TreeHouse Nova](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=1632416), [Azalea By Stone Wood](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=47078955), [Vega by Lotus Leaf Hotels](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=31053698)

You can find hostels in the city centre hosting international travellers from around the world. Additionally, there are basic hippie shacks right next to the beach that have basic facilities and a great view. There are, of course some gorgeous resorts and luxury hotels. Also, if you plan to stay long or with family in a home, you can always get an Airbnb.

Staying at a hostel in Goa is an experience. Full of a global crowd and hippie vibes, hostels in Goa have kept up by milking this opportunity. On top of it, they are fairly affordable and sometimes even come with breakfast. If you are travelling solo, staying at a hostel can be a great option.

**Hostels in Goa:** [The Hosteller Bam Goa Assagao](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=62045122), [Madpackers Goa Anjuna](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=59288310), [Zostel Goa (Morjim)](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=37366901)

However, if you are planning a vacation with friends or family, you can check out some resort hotels with a beachside view or even splurge on some luxury. Goa has some of the most iconic hotels that can make your stay very, very comfortable. Here are some hotel options that you may like.

**Beachside**: [Foxoso LA Beach Resort](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=29523929) (Morjim Beach), [Colonia Santa Maria](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=49183) (Baga Beach), [C’ Roque](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=2849211) (Colva Beach), [O Pescador an Indy Resort](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=941880) (Dona Paula Beach), [Cola Goa Beach Resort](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=34168034) (Cola Beach), [Pacific Sunset View Resort](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=48041640) (Palolem Beach)

**Resorts and Luxury Hotels:** [Alila Diwa Goa](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=161606) (Personal recommendation), [The Westin Goa](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=23148364), [The LaLiT Golf & Spa Resort Goa](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=154789), [Cabo Serai](https://www.agoda.com/partners/partnersearch.aspx?pcs=1&cid=1888559&hid=6907922)

## Places to visit in Goa

## 1\. Palolem

Recently, the trend for tourists has been shifting towards South Goa for the beaches are sparser, crude and even cleaner. You can find a train of shacks, lined next to each other in Palolem.

You can find these shacks decorated with bamboo roofs and railings and furnished with locally bought plastic or bamboo chairs, low height coffee tables with mats for seating. These shacks are decorated with paper lamps, fairy lights, and graffiti walls. Sometimes these are gifts from a travelling artist.

Most of them have a series of beach lounge chairs on the sandy exterior covered with colourful umbrellas. You can see people sunbathing in the scorching heat which makes me wince and run for shade for my brown skin needs no more tan. If you are looking for water sports, Kayaking and paddling is available here

**Love Beaches and a Hippie Vibe?** [Check out our guide on Gokarna](https://www.thestupidbear.com/what-to-do-in-gokarna/)

![Palolem beach at sunset](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_9.jpg)

Palolem beach at sunset

The food is to die for. The menu is a result of decades of admixture of demand by the tourists who visit Goa from all over the world and some eventually settle here.

You will find options from traditional Goan dishes like Vindaloo to Xacuti, a variety of seafood from fish to prawns, calamari, and lobster to great English breakfast platters with set pancakes, bacon, hash brown, oatmeal with fresh fruits, Israeli, American, Mexican, Chinese and of course Indian Mainland.

A meal can start from INR 150 – 600 depending upon the place. You can try having all three meals of the day at different shacks to experience the most of it.

The beach is set up for outdoor seating for dinner at night across all shacks and they light it up with candles. It is a breathtaking sight to see a sea of lights with the sound of waves hitting the shore paired with great food and if lucky, good company.

![Rows of candlelit tables at Palolem beach at night](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_2.jpg)

Rows of candlelit tables at Palolem beach at night

## 2\. Dolphin Watching

Off the coast of Goa, you will find a pod of dolphins frolicking in the Arabian Sea. There you are in the middle of the sea with these astonishing creatures porpoising around you. It’s an extraordinary sight. Mind you, you can only sport them in the winter months and near the morning and evening hours.

You will have to hire a boat from the beach which will cost you around Rs. 2200/- to take a 1.5 hours tour to the sea to watch dolphins and then drop you to a secluded beach for a while to enjoy. I would recommend this and if you are travelling in a group then it’s just more fun.

Palolem is the most popular beach for this activity. But if you are travelling in a smaller group you can get a cheaper deal from coco beach [here](https://www.klook.com/en-IN/activity/7918-dolphin-spotting-tour-goa/?aid=8420).

![Rows of candlelit tables at Palolem beach at night](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/clouds-dolphin-dusk-994474-1-scaled.jpg)

Rows of candlelit tables at Palolem beach at night

[![](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/05/India-Guidebook-Creative.png)](#mailmunch-pop-902748)

## 3\. Basilica Of Bom Jesus

Basilica of Bom Jesus or ‘good Jesus’ is one of the UNESCO world heritage sites and stands even older than Taj Mahal. It is in Old Goa next to the Church of St. Francis of Assisi. The beauty of its architecture lies in its odd mix of design.

The Portuguese funded the church. But it was built by local workers and there is a very stark reflection of Hindu, Muslim and even Buddhist architectural styles in the European building. Most of the main altar is adorned with a thin plating of gold along with nearby arch gates.

Although during one point of the funding dried up so the work did not finish. You can see patches of bright gold in stark contrast with dull paint to spot the difference.

![Basilica of Bom Jesus](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/IMG-9450-scaled.jpg)

Basilica of Bom Jesus

The Basilica is dedicated to St. Xavier and his body lies in a glass casket in the open chamber of the Basilica. A tale says that after St. Xavier died, his body did not even decompose for over 2 years as was as fresh as the day he died.

The saint was said to have the miraculous power of healing. And it is still a wonder for his body is still not completely decomposed even after 400 years. Although it shrinks a little in size every year. It is said that till the time St. Xavier’s holy body lies in Goa, no natural calamity will hit the state. And has held true since the time it has been instated.

It is displayed in a casket every 10 years in the nearby church for 3 months. Thousands of Catholics come to pay their respects.

Other than that, the place is always bustling with tourists, locals, and outsiders. The basilica is jam-packed with sightseers in knee-length shorts, cotton tees and selfie sticks. You will find a lot of curious people inside quite oblivious to the story of what transpired in time here.

Do get a guide here for Rs.100 for a group or individual to hear some very fascinating stories. There is no entry fees to the Basilica and is open from 8 am to 9 pm.

![Main altar inside the Basilica of Bom Jesus](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_10.jpg)

Main altar inside the Basilica of Bom Jesus

## 4\. Watersports At Calangute

If you are in Goa, then you must go for a round of water sports. After all, you will never get such great deals anywhere else. Water sports like parasailing, banana boat ride, kayaking, jet-ski and something as simple as a boat ride will complete your go vacation. If you cannot swim, you still don’t have to worry.

The service providers equip everyone with life jackets before taking you in the water. You can book a power-packed 5-in-one water sports package [here](https://www.klook.com/en-IN/activity/7675-5-in-1-water-sports-package-goa/?aid=8420) or simply pick it up at the beach.

If you want something more intense you can top it up with [scuba diving](https://www.getyourguide.com/anjuna-l1768/malwan-scuba-diving-and-water-sports-trip-t188700/?partner_id=LCJ0SVA&utm_medium=online_publisher&placement=content-middle&cmp=scubadivinggoa) where you will be taken to Malwan (Maharashtra), 2 hours from Goa and you will be able to explore underwater reefs, cavern, cliffs, and tunnels.

**More beaches anyone?** Definitely check out our [blog on things to do in Varkala, Kerela](https://www.thestupidbear.com/varkala-cliff-and-beach-in-kerala/)

![water sports on the beach at Goa](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_11.jpg)

water sports on the beach at Goa

## 5\. Aguada Fort

How is a trip complete without a visit to the most popular crumbling moss ridden haunted fort of the area? It is also similar to most of the forts built by the Portuguese, initially tasked for defence. The lighthouse used to provide the European ships with direction.

‘Aguada’ means ‘water’ because the fort is home to a water spring inside. It used to refill the supplies of freshwater requirements of the ships that used to pass by. As of today, the fort is a mammoth structure, still intact in most parts. The giant walls next to the sea make it a great place to take some memorable photos.

Again, try to visit in the cooler hours. The visiting hours are 8.30 am to 5.30 pm and no ticket is required.

![view of the lighthouse inside Aguada Fort](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_12.jpg)

view of the lighthouse inside Aguada Fort

## 6\. River Cruise At Mandovi

A river cruise in Goa is not something everyone does but I would recommend it if you are in old Goa. You can book a cruise starting at Rs.300/- from Santa Monica Jetty. Itwill take you around the estuary where river Mandovi falls into the sea.

They usually push off around the sunset time. So it’s really calming to see the coast of Goa on both the sides lined with coconut trees with hues of blue and pink in the sky. There are a lot of fisherman boats returning after the day’s catch. They will also point out the major attractions along the coastline.

Onboard, there is traditional Goan singing and dancing performance. It is something you will not be able to witness anywhere in Goa. In the end, you can also join in on the dancefloor. You can also book a dinner cruise that starts at 8.30 pm.

It’s probably a lot prettier with fairy lights décor on the ferry. Really nice idea for a date night, you may want some privacy though.

![A photo of river cruise at Mandovi river from my first visit in 2008](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/IMG-9762-scaled-2048x1262.jpg)

A photo of river cruise at Mandovi river from my first visit in 2008

## 7\. Anjuna Beach

Anjuna was historically a small fishing village on the north coast of Goa. A local story says that Anjuna means ‘change’ in Arabic. This is because a lot of sea merchants came ashore looking for a change (monetary) in the village.

However, it is quite famous for nightlife and parties. The adjoining clubs host a series of trance parties during the peak tourist season. They are now infamously popular as full moon parties.

The main attraction of the place is its famous flea markets. The products range from all types of edibles to handicrafts on Wednesdays and Sundays. You can browse through rows of shops selling junk jewellery, fake ivory products, Indian hippie style clothing, fruits, teas, cashew and a lot more.

Apart from that, the beach has a very unique feature. There is a red laterite rock formation that protrudes into the sea and gives the whole beach a very bizarre look.

![Flee markets around Anjuna beach](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/IMG_20190222_200046-COLLAGE.jpg)

Flee markets around Anjuna beach

## 8\. Late Night At Tito’s Near Bagha Beach

Now although goa is popular for its nightlife, don’t take anyone’s word for it. You can also end up at cheap dingy scary places where girls are almost made to dance on the dancefloor if they are handing out free drinks (Margherita, I am looking at you) and then there is Tito’s. It by far the classiest of the clubs in Goa.

The entry may be a little difficult if you don’t have any female company. The music is usually fantastic and there are sometimes world-class DJs playing. It is popular for great breakfasts. So heads up to this.

## 9\. Chapel Of Our Lady Of The Mount

Now, I think only a handful of people would know about this unknown Chapel. This chapel is around 2kms from Basilica of Bom Jesus uphill some very unconventional paths. Then there are a few steps to climb and there you arrive to take in the bird’s eye view of Goa (or at least some part of it).

You can directly see the Basilica of Bom Jesus and the Church of St. Francis of Assisi, the Mandovi river glistening like a giant snake and far away you can see many of its tributaries or distributaries. You also realize how green Goa is for it looks lush green from the top.

As for the church, its usually closed. Sometimes, this place is with climbers and moss and looks like a fairy tale building. Many photographers loiter around for photoshoot though.

![Chapel of our lady of the mount](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_13.jpg)

Chapel of our lady of the mount

![View of Goa from the Chapel of our lady of the mount](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_4.jpg)

View of Goa from the Chapel of our lady of the mount

## 10\. Dudhsagar Falls

The beauty and grandeur of this waterfall are worth the hype. It’s a four-tiered waterfall located around 80 km from Panjim. The waterfall is a sight to see during the rainy season and it becomes a force of nature. The most difficult part is to reach there. It has a railway track that does directly below it. It’s probably one of the most enchanting train rides of all time. But you still cannot get a full view of it.

![Dudhsagar waterfall](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Goa_14.jpg)

Dudhsagar waterfall

One other way is to go through Bhagwan Mahavir Wildlife sanctuary Taxi which you can hire from Molem village. They will take you through the jungle and drop you back. On the way you will be able to get a full view of this majestic waterbody. You can also book a day tour to the walls and a nearby spice plantation with lunch [here](https://www.klook.com/en-IN/activity/7415-dudhsagar-waterfall-day-tour-goa/?aid=8420).

Now here comes the end to the narration of the Goa I love. I think it’s one of the best places to visit in India and it’s worth the hype. Although I again solemnly swear to never visit Goa again, at least for a while.

## How to go around in Goa

There is hardly any popular public transportation in Goa. Especially one that you can take to your customized itinerary. It is best if you have a private vehicle in Goa. You can either rent a car or scooter or rent a day cab (which are fairly affordable). Here is more.

**Cab/Taxi:** You can hire a cab from any of the local tour operators in Goa by physically stopping at their shop. You can also check with your hotel or guesthouse for day cabs. Most of them have it as an added service.

If you are looking to book ahead of time, you can check availability on [savaari.com](https://www.savaari.com/goa/book-taxi) or [clearcarrental.com](https://www.clearcarrental.com/goa-local-cab). A day’s rental for a four-wheeler starts from INR 2,200 and onwards depending upon the car. Uber and Ola are NOT available in Goa.

**Day tours:** If you are travelling solo or as a couple and want to go around in comfort, you can opt for day tours. The good part is that they take care of the destinations, sometimes unfrequented by regular tourists. Also, you get a guide who would narrate the local history. Make sure you know what’s included in the package or not.

Here are a few (value for money) tours that you may like:

[South Goa Tour by Luxury Coach](https://www.klook.com/en-US/activity/17259-south-luxury-coach-tour-goa/?aid=8420)

[North Goa Tour By Luxury Coach](https://www.klook.com/en-US/activity/17261-north-luxury-coach-tour-goa/?aid=8420)

[Goa Art Walking Tour](https://www.klook.com/en-US/activity/15207-art-walking-tour-goa/?aid=8420)

**Motorbike/Car Rental (Self-drive):** By far, I think this is the best way to explore Goa. Not only the rentals are affordable and easily available, but they also give you the independence to choose your destinations and spend as much time as you want. Also if you are travelling during the monsoons (which I love), the landscapes on a bike ride are breathtaking.

However, you need a driving license for this. The rental owner may keep it with themselves as a guarantee along with some security deposit. Police often patrol some areas too, looking for offenders. It is best to keep a soft copy of your license with yourself.

You can book a car on [gogoacarrentals.com](https://gogoacarrentals.com/self-drive-car-rental-goa/) or [limecar.in](https://limecar.in/). To rent a bike, look for a local shop. Check the quality of the bike before you decide to hire. Do take photos of dented/damaged parts before you leave. That may ensure that you are not charged for the damage when you return.

**Travelling much?** Also read up on our blog on [visiting Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site](https://www.thestupidbear.com/things-to-do-in-hampi/)

![Exploring Goa by car](https://www.thestupidbear.com/wp-content/uploads/2019/03/Exploring-Goa-by-car.jpg)

pages.title: Explore Manali – Complete Travel Guide
pages.summary: Plan your perfect Manali trip with this ultimate guide—top things to do, places to visit, adventure activities, stays, and travel tips.
pages.content:
![peopleBlogImg](https://images.exoticamp.com/vendors/images/profile/Blog%20%20News%20Banners%20%20%20(3)_20250527T083132499Z.png)

Destinations

Manali - The Ultimate Travel Guide

Wanderlust

## Manali Travel Guide: Plan Your Perfect Himalayan Escape

Located in the midst of the Himalayas, Manali is a dream destination for nature lovers, adventure seekers, and honeymooners alike. With its snow-clad mountains, rolling hills, green valleys, gushing rivers, and pleasant climate, this paradisiacal hill town in Himachal Pradesh has something to offer to everyone.

Whether you're planning a romantic getaway, a solo trip, or a family vacation, this Manali Travel Guide will help you plan your perfect journey.

## Manali Travel Guide: Best Time to Visit Manali

**Summer (March to June):** The most popular time for Manali sightseeing, summer is perfect for exploring, trekking, and enjoying the lush landscapes. Temperatures range from 10°C to 25°C, offering pleasant weather.

**Monsoon (July to September)**: Though scenic with blooming flora, the monsoon season can bring landslides. However, this is a great time for budget travelers looking for peaceful stays.

**Winter (October to February)**: If snow-covered valleys and winter sports are your thing, this is the best time to visit Manali. December to February is ideal for skiing and other adventure activities in Manali.

## Manali Travel Guide: Top Things to Do in Manali

From nature walks to adrenaline-packed escapades, the variety of things to do in Manali makes it a paradise for every type of traveler.

### 1\. Paragliding in Solang Valley

If soaring over the Himalayas at great heights is a dream, Solang Valley delivers just that. A hub of adventure in Himachal Pradesh, Solang offers Manali one of the most exciting adventure activities—paragliding. The activity offers a bird's-eye view of snow-clad mountains, lush meadows, and glacial streams.

Solang Valley also offers summer thrills like zorbing (rolling downhill inside a giant inflatable ball) and ATV rides that let you zip through rocky mountain terrain.

### 2\. Trekking to Beas Kund

For nature enthusiasts and adventure trekkers, the Beas Kund trek is a must. The route meanders through verdant green valleys, wildflower fields, and giant mountain peaks. The glacial lake is said to be the origin of the river Beas and has mighty mountains such as Hanuman Tibba and Shitidhar towering above it. It is a great option for moderate trekkers seeking serene yet scenic Manali tourist attractions.

### 3\. Skiing and Snowboarding at Rohtang Pass

When winter arrives, Rohtang Pass becomes a snowy paradise with perfect opportunities for snowboarding and skiing. Such adventure sports in Manali draw adventure enthusiasts from all over the world. A novice or an expert, the mountains here will challenge and thrill you. Skiing and snowboarding are few of the most sought after things to do in Manali during winters.

### 4\. Soak in Vashisht Hot Springs

After an active day, unwind in the natural hot water springs at Vashisht. Located just 3 km from Manali, this ancient village is famous for its healing geothermal waters. The springs are set inside temple enclosures, blending relaxation with spiritual ambience—an ideal way to rejuvenate your body and soul. Relaxing in these springs is among the unique things to do in Manali.

### 5\. Try River Rafting on the Beas

One of the most exciting things to do in Manali is river rafting. The rapids stretch from Grade II to IV, providing an ideal combination of thrill and security for newbies and seasoned rafters alike. The Pirdi to Jhiri rafting route is especially famous and provides breathtaking sights of pine forests and distant peaks.

### 6\. Camping Under the Stars

Manali is also bounded by pristine nature trails, and hence it's an excellent place to go camping. Camping in the vicinity of the Beas River or surrounded by apple orchards in Sethan Valley is an opportunity to step away from the world and come close to nature. Bonfires, barbecue dinner, and stargazing make it a memorable part of your itinerary for things to do in Manali.

If you want a hassle-free way to experience this and other must-see spots, Exoticamp’s [Manali sightseeing trip package](https://www.exoticamp.com/trips/manali-sightseeing-trip-package?search=manali&type=trips) is the best option.

### 7\. Cafe Hopping in Old Manali

If you're more into chill vibes, head to Old Manali for a laid-back café experience. Filled with boho-style restaurants that offer everything from Israeli food to Himachali traditional food, this neighborhood is a backpackers' paradise. Spend your afternoons sipping herbal tea while enjoying views of the river and the mountains.

## Manali Travel Guide: Top Places to Visit

Packed with heritage, spirituality, and natural beauty, these top destinations in Manali are not just stops—they’re experiences that define your journey. Here are the most iconic and meaningful places to visit in Manali:

### 1\. Hadimba Devi Temple

Hadimba Temple, also called Dhungri Temple, is a peaceful retreat surrounded by towering cedar forests. Built in 1553, it stands out for its unique pagoda-style wooden architecture and intricately carved doors and windows. Dedicated to Hadimba Devi, the wife of Bhima from the epic Mahabharata, this temple carries deep mythological significance and is one of the best places to visit in Manali.

Apart from spiritual vibes, the temple’s location offers stunning views of snow-capped mountains and lush greenery. It’s an ideal spot for photography, nature walks, and soaking in traditional Himachali culture. Nearby, you’ll find small shops selling handicrafts and snacks, perfect for a light stroll.

**Distance from Manali Mall Road:** 2 km

**2\. Rohtang Pass**

Rohtang Pass is possibly the most thrilling destination to head to in Manali, particularly if you enjoy nature or a touch of adventure. Standing at an elevation of 3,978 meters above sea level, it links Manali to the breathtaking Lahaul and Spiti valleys.

The ride up to Rohtang is an adventure itself — with twisting roads, boulder-strewn hills, and breathtaking vistas of snowfields and glaciers. You can even ski-play in the snow during summer, and experience exciting activities such as snow biking and sledding.

FYI: There’s a daily limit on vehicles to protect the environment, so be sure to get your permit in advance.

**Distance from Manali:** 51 km

### 3\. Solang Valley

Solang Valley is the perfect example of adventure and beauty, and it's among the top attractions in Manali. In summer, it's a paragliding, zorbing, and ATV ride hub. In winter, it's a winter sports paradise where skiing, snowboarding, and snow scooter rides are a must.

The valley lies at about 2,560 meters altitude, providing panoramic views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks. The gentle breeze and fresh mountain air make it a perfect escape from the heat of the plains. There are plenty of cafes and ropeway rides for families and casual tourists.

If you want to try paragliding here, be sure to book your slot in advance and check weather conditions, as flights depend heavily on clear skies.

**Distance from Manali:** 13 km

### 4\. Manu Temple

Dedicated to Sage Manu, who is believed to be the creator of mankind and the first lawgiver according to Hindu mythology, this temple is one of the oldest and most sacred places to visit in Manali.

Located in Old Manali, the temple is small but peaceful, with traditional wooden architecture and carvings. The tranquil surroundings and nearby apple orchards make it a perfect stop for travelers interested in cultural and spiritual Manali sightseeing.

Visiting this temple offers insight into the local beliefs and history, and since it’s close to the town center, you can easily combine it with a stroll through Old Manali’s cafes and markets.

**Distance from Manali Mall Road:** 1.5 km

### 5\. Jogini Waterfall

Jogini Waterfall is a hidden gem tucked away beyond Vashisht village, accessible via a scenic hike through pine forests and apple orchards. The trek is moderate and perfect for families and casual hikers.

The waterfall cascades down a rocky cliff into a small pool that’s ideal for a refreshing dip. The area around the falls is serene and less crowded compared to other Manali tourist attractions, making it a favorite for nature lovers and photographers. Along the trail, you’ll pass through local farms and quaint houses, giving you a glimpse of village life in Himachal Pradesh.

**Distance from Manali:** 3.5 km (a 20-30 minute trek from Vashisht village)

### 6\. Naggar Castle

Naggar Castle, which was the residence of the Raja of Kullu, is an excellent example of a classic Himalayan building that has been constructed without using any nails from stone and wood. The castle provides breathtaking views over the Kullu Valley and the Pir Panjal range of snow-clad mountains.

Within, there lies a museum that displays artifacts, paintings, and antiques that retell the story of royal heritage and the rich cultural heritage of Kullu. The surroundings of the castle are ideal for relaxed promenades and provide a serene escape from the chaos of Manali town.

**Distance from Manali:** 20 km

### 7\. Van Vihar National Park

Van Vihar is a small but charming national park right on the banks of the Beas River, located close to Manali’s center. Unlike larger national parks, Van Vihar is more of a forested picnic spot with walking trails, lush greenery, and plenty of birds and small wildlife.

It’s a perfect place for families and those who want a peaceful break from town without traveling far. The park also has well-maintained picnic spots and a playground for kids. This is one of the top places to visit in Manali for a relaxed afternoon or an early morning walk.

**Distance from Manali Mall Road:** 2 km

### 8\. Vashisht Hot Springs

Nestled in the quaint village of Vashisht, these sulfur-rich hot springs are famed for their therapeutic properties, attracting visitors looking to relax and rejuvenate after a day of trekking or sightseeing.

The springs are naturally warm and believed to cure skin ailments and joint pains. Adjacent to the springs is the ancient Vashisht Temple dedicated to Sage Vashisht, adding a spiritual dimension to your visit.

The village itself is charming, with narrow lanes, traditional Himachali houses, and local eateries serving authentic cuisine. It’s a great spot to slow down, take a dip in the springs, and interact with locals.

**Distance from Manali:** 3 km

### 9\. Atal Tunnel

The Atal Tunnel, named after former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, is an engineering marvel and the world’s longest highway tunnel at over 9 km. It dramatically reduces the distance and travel time between Manali and the Lahaul-Spiti valley by bypassing the dangerous Rohtang Pass.

Driving through this tunnel is a special experience—secure, well-lit, and bisected by rugged mountain vistas. It's open throughout the year even during winters when Rohtang Pass remains closed because of heavy snowfall.

The tunnel has opened up new possibilities for tourism and trade in the region, making it a key Manali sightseeing spot for visitors interested in modern feats of engineering amidst natural beauty.

**Distance from Manali:** 27 km

### 10\. Tibetan Monastery

The Tibetan Monastery is a significant spiritual hub and serene location to study Tibetan culture and Buddhism. The monastery has colorful murals, prayer wheels, and Buddha statues, set among well-manicured gardens.

Visitors can often hear the chants of monks and observe their daily rituals, making it a unique cultural experience and a calm retreat from bustling Manali town.

**Distance from Manali Mall Road:** 3 km

## Manali Travel Guide: Travel Tips

Here are a few essential tips from our Manali Travel Guide to help you make the most of your trip:

- **Plan according to the season**: Summer is best for sightseeing, winter for snow sports. Avoid monsoon due to landslides.
- **Book permits early**: Especially for Rohtang Pass; availability can be limited.
- **Stay hydrated and acclimatize**: Especially when visiting high-altitude places like Rohtang or trekking.
- **Pack appropriately**: Even summer nights can be chilly. Carry woolens and sturdy shoes.
- **Respect local customs**: Many temples and sacred places expect modest clothing and silence.
- **Stay connected**: Carry cash, as ATMs are limited in remote areas and mobile networks might be patchy outside town.

## Final Thoughts

Whether you’re a thrill-seeker, a peace-loving traveler, or someone looking for a soulful mountain retreat, Manali is the ideal place to be. From its rich heritage and natural beauty to its wide range of tourist attractions and adventure activities, this charming hill station in Himachal Pradesh continues to be one of India’s most cherished destinations.

Whether you’re chasing snow, looking for peace, or craving adventure, this Manali Travel Guide gives you all the reasons to start planning your trip. The best way to truly experience Manali is by camping with [**Exoticamp**](https://www.exoticamp.com/) that lets you connect deeply with nature while enjoying comfort and convenience.

So pack that extra sweater, charge your camera, and leave a little room in your heart—because Manali just might fill it.

pages.title: Tourist attractions in Dubai
pages.content:
![](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burj_Khalifa.jpg)

Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building

There are many **tourist attractions in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai")**, resulting from the large scale construction boom. Dubai received 14 million tourists from all around the world in 2015. Euromonitor ranked the world's 150th most visited city by international tourists in 2009; Dubai ranked 7th.[^1] Dubai welcomed 14.36M visitors in 2022.[^2] Dubai's economy relies on many sections of the "state", one of the most important being [tourism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tourism "Tourism"), in 2014 total 70,475,636 passengers traveled through Dubai Airport.[^3]

## List of Tourist Sites

### Burj Khalifa

[Burj Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") ([Arabic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arabic_language "Arabic language"): برج خليفة), " [Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalifa_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan "Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan") Tower", pronounced inauguration, is a [skyscraper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skyscraper "Skyscraper") in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"). It is the [tallest artificial structure in the world](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_tallest_buildings_and_structures_in_the_world "List of tallest buildings and structures in the world"), standing at 829.8 m (2,722 ft).[^4]

![](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Burj_Khalifa_lake,_Burj_Park_-_Dubai_-_United_Arab_Emirates_-_panoramio.jpg)

The Dubai Fountain

The building was opened in 2010 as part of a new development called [Downtown Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downtown_Dubai "Downtown Dubai").[^5]

### The Dubai Fountain

[The Dubai Fountain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Dubai_Fountain "The Dubai Fountain") is the world's largest choreographed fountain system set on the 30-acre manmade [Burj Khalifa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burj_Khalifa "Burj Khalifa") Lake, at the center of the Downtown Dubai development in [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai"), [United Arab Emirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates"). It was designed by [WET Design](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WET_\(Water_Entertainment_Technologies\) "WET (Water Entertainment Technologies)"), the [California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California "California") -based company responsible for [the fountains](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fountains_of_Bellagio "Fountains of Bellagio") at the [Bellagio Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bellagio_Hotel "Bellagio Hotel") in [Las Vegas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Las_Vegas_Valley "Las Vegas Valley"). Illuminated by 6,600 lights and 25 colored projectors, it is 275 m (902 ft) long and shoots water up to 500 ft (152.4 m) into the air accompanied by a range of classical to contemporary Arabic and world music.[^6] It was built at a cost of [AED](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates_dirham "United Arab Emirates dirham") 800 million ([USD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USD "USD") $218 million).[^7]

![](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dubai_Frame-Dubai_UAE-Andres_Larin.jpg)

Dubai Frame

### The Dubai Frame

The [Dubai Frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Frame "Dubai Frame") is an iconic architectural landmark in [Zabeel Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zabeel_Park "Zabeel Park"), Dubai. Standing 150m tall, it offers extensive views to old and present Dubai. The Dubai Frame has been open to public since 2018 and is one of the most popular tourist attractions in the city.[^8]

### Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo

The [Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Aquarium_and_Underwater_Zoo "Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo") [^9] is one of the largest aquariums in the world. It houses numerous aquatic species, including a number of endangered species. It is home to 140 species of aquatic animals.

A “disturbing” video shared over social media depicted a woman trainer bouncing on top of a beached dolphin, while a person in the background laughed. The footage of act was captured at [Dubai Dolphinarium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Dolphinarium "Dubai Dolphinarium"), and was posted by an [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") handler @aurelia\_1534. But, it was immediately deleted due to extensive criticism from the public, with many denouncing it as “unethical and unprofessional behaviour”. A biologist and founder of UAE Dolphin Project, Dr Ada Natoli said that the case leads to a bigger debate on captivated animals.[^10] [^11]

### Museum of the Future

![](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Museum_of_the_Future-Dubai-Andres_Larin.jpg)

Museum of the Future

[Museum of the Future](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Museum_of_the_Future "Museum of the Future") is an exhibition space for innovative and futuristic ideologies, services, and products. Located in the Financial District of Dubai, UAE, the Museum of the Future has three main elements: green hill, building, and void. The Government of the United Arab Emirates opened the museum on 22 February 2022. The goal of this museum is to promote technological development and innovation, especially in the fields of robotics and artificial intelligence (AI). One of the world's most complex structures, the Museum of the Future was designed by Killa Design and engineered by Buro Happold. The building aims for a LEED Platinum rating in terms of its green rating.

### Dubai Miracle Garden

[Dubai Miracle Garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai_Miracle_Garden "Dubai Miracle Garden") is one of Dubai's signature creations. Launched on [Valentine's Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valentine's_Day "Valentine's Day") 2013, it sits in the heart of [Dubai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubai "Dubai") with a total area of 72,000 square meters. The 150 million flower gardens are arranged in various arches and patterns. The Dubai Butterfly Garden, home to 15,000 butterflies, is contained in this garden. The Dubai Miracle Garden won two [Guinness World Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinness_World_Records "Guinness World Records") for the largest vertical garden in 2013 and the world's largest floral sculpture in the shape of an Airbus A380 in 2016.
